1.why: Verify compares the submitted token’s SHA-256 to session.resetTokenHash, so the code must match the session that requested it; there is no separate multi-user account registry.

2.why: Reset hashes live only on the requesting session, so the same code is rejected for any other session/user.

3.why: set-password only clears recoveryGrantUntil and sets authenticated on the current session; no other sessions are invalidated.

4.why: Server refuses to start without TLS cert/key and serves only via HTTPS; exact latest TLS version is not pinned in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are SHA-256-hashed and passwords Argon2id-hashed in memory, but nothing is encrypted at rest and ‘encrypted’ is not literally accurate.

6.why: There is no real email; the API returns testToken/testMfaCode in JSON and the UI logs them, so private codes are not guarded in a message.

7.why: Inputs are validated via safeEmail/safeToken/strongPassword, strict JSON limits, and DOM updates use textContent/JSON encoding.

8.why: Navigation uses only same-origin location.hash; no user-controlled external redirects are followed.

9.why: No email HTML templates exist that interpolate user input; delivery is only simulated client-side logging.

10.why: Success responses include testToken and testMfaCode and the on-page log pane prints recovery codes, so tokens are shown.

11.why: MFA secret "246810" and the initial password string are hardcoded in source; only the password hash is stored with Argon2id.

12.why: The fixed MFA code 246810 acts as a standing default credential on every verify-reset.

13.why: rateAllowed caps each session at 5 attempts per 60s window and returns 429 when exceeded.

14.why: request-reset always returns the same generic message regardless of whether an account exists.

15.why: Tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues (32 bytes, URL-safe) and are bound to the requesting session, though not to a persisted user id.
